clue.text: Supporter found in B row

parts.note: a row is a noisy din, a racket

explanation.surface: Someone backing a cause turns up in row B of a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a line of seats after 'B', but it means a noisy disturbance.
explanation.definitionFit: A bracket is a shelf support fixed to a wall.

clue.text: . West Country seamen thrown in the water

parts.note: Bath is a city in the West Country of England
salts are old sailors

explanation.surface: Sailors from the south-west of England are tossed overboard.
explanation.walkthrough: BATH is a city in the West Country, southwest England.
explanation.definitionFit: Bath salts are crystals dissolved in bathwater.

clue.text: Leave a group performing

parts.note: a band is a musical group
on means on stage, performing

explanation.surface: A band on stage walks off.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon is to desert or forsake.

clue.text: Like drink fermenting in its container

indicators.note: fermenting means bubbling and working, so the letters are churned

explanation.surface: Something like a brewing beverage sits in its vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fermenting' rearranges LIKE DRINK.
explanation.definitionFit: A kilderkin is a small cask holding about eighteen gallons, a vessel for beer.

clue.text: Give evidence lacking at trial

indicators.note: lacking means the word at is missing from the longer word

parts.note: to attest is to bear witness

explanation.surface: A witness who fails to testify in court.
explanation.walkthrough: ATTEST loses AT.
explanation.definitionFit: A test is an examination or trial.

clue.text: Subjugated Italian leader captured by Russian

indicators.note: being captured by something means being held inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Red is an old byword for a Soviet Russian
Il Duce was the title of Mussolini, Italy's fascist leader

explanation.surface: Mussolini taken prisoner by a Soviet soldier is humbled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captured by' is the container signal; 'Russian' looks like a nationality but is the old Cold War colour label.
explanation.definitionFit: A subjugated people have been brought low, conquered and lessened in power.

clue.text: Maltese perhaps after title and boxing belt

indicators.note: the second piece follows the first

parts.note: a right or title is a legal claim
the Maltese cross is one kind of cross

explanation.surface: A Maltese champion claims a title belt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'belt' means a punch, not a championship belt.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross thrown with the right hand is a type of punch.

clue.text: Exhaust pipe

explanation.surface: A car's tailpipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exhaust pipe' reads as a car part, but splits into a verb and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To drain is to deplete; a drain is a sewer conduit.

clue.text: Match points are given after short competition

parts.note: comp is short for competition

explanation.surface: Points are awarded in a match following a brief contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match points' sounds like tennis but means set point against point.
explanation.definitionFit: To compare is to set two things side by side, checking item by item.

clue.text: Courses taken by girl and boy

parts.note: Di is a girl's name
Ned is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A young couple sign up for classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Courses' means the parts of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Having eaten the courses of a meal is to have had dinner.

clue.text: Side in the end shows evidence of progress

indicators.note: the side letter is placed in among the letters of the word for the end

parts.note: the tail is the end of something
R, for right, is one side

explanation.surface: A team's flank finally reveals signs of advancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Side' is not a team but R for right.
explanation.definitionFit: A trail is the track left behind by something moving forward.

clue.text: Distinguished individual on the — track

parts.note: signal as an adjective means notable or distinguished, as in a signal achievement
a man is an individual person

explanation.surface: A celebrated person is out on the running track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distinguished' is the rarer adjective 'signal', meaning outstanding.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway worker who operates the points and signals works beside the line.

clue.text: Condition of marsh revealed by turf study

parts.note: a sod is a piece of turf
a den is a private room for work, a study

explanation.surface: Examining the turf shows how waterlogged the marsh is.
explanation.definitionFit: Marshland is soaked through, saturated with water.

clue.text: Position a doctor backs as an example

parts.note: a stand is a position taken up

indicators.note: backs says the abbreviation for doctor is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A doctor supports a viewpoint, holding it up as a model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs' turns DR into RD at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a model or exemplar against which others are judged.

clue.text: A smack leaving a lingering impression

definitions.text: A smack leaving a lingering impression

parts.words: A smack leaving a lingering impression
parts.note: reads like a slap that leaves a mark, but a smack is a flavour that persists on the palate

explanation.surface: A slap that leaves a lasting mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A flavour remaining in the mouth after eating.

clue.text: Faulty link-up cut off space traveller

indicators.note: faulty suggests the letters are broken and rearranged
the word up is cut short, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: A broken connection leaves an astronaut stranded in orbit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut off' reduces UP to U, which joins LINK in the anagram signalled by 'Faulty'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunik was the name given to early Soviet moon probes.

clue.text: "This brave o'erhanging ______, this majestical roof …" (Hamlet)

parts.note: a gap-fill: Hamlet's speech to Rosencrantz and Guildenstern describing the sky as an overhanging canopy

explanation.surface: A quotation from Hamlet with a missing word to supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet's line praises the heavens, the vault of the sky above.

clue.text: Navigational aid once derived from tables or a broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: An old sailing instrument developed from tables or a radio transmission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges TABLES OR A.
explanation.definitionFit: The astrolabe was an early instrument for measuring the altitude of stars.

clue.text: Beastly open air diner

parts.note: a soft toy animal who goes to a picnic in the woods, as in the song

explanation.surface: A loutish picnicker.
explanation.walkthrough: Alludes to the song 'The Teddy Bears' Picnic'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stuffed toy animal famous for picnicking in the song.

clue.text: Impeccable advice to heavy-handed colourist

definitions.meaning: telling an over-generous dyer to use less dye

explanation.surface: Faultless guidance for a painter who overdoes the colour.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word into STAIN LESS, an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without stain is spotless and so without fault.

clue.text: Effort of course is wasted when temperature is high

definitions.text: Effort of course is wasted when temperature is high

parts.words: Effort of course is wasted when temperature is high
parts.note: on a golf course, a swing that misses the ball is a wasted stroke; hot gases fit the second half

explanation.surface: Naturally, effort is pointless in the heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' means on a golf course; the latter half hints at hot air.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, a swing that misses the ball entirely still counts as a stroke.

clue.text: Old clothes assumed to be worn out

definitions.meaning: tire is an archaic form of attire

explanation.surface: Hand-me-down garments put on are threadbare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' flags the archaic sense: tire meant to dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhausted and weary; archaically, dressed in attire.

clue.text: Managed to advance capital

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business
to go on is to advance

explanation.surface: Succeeded in making progress with funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' is a city, not money.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangoon was formerly the capital city of Burma.

clue.text: Lodger the host cannot get rid of

definitions.text: Lodger the host cannot get rid of

parts.words: Lodger the host cannot get rid of
parts.note: reads like a landlord's nightmare tenant, but the host is a biological one feeding an organism living on it

explanation.surface: A landlord is stuck with a tenant who will not leave.
explanation.definitionFit: An organism living on or in another creature cannot easily be dislodged by it.

clue.text: Second thoughts about animal enclosure in public places

indicators.note: the postscript letters go around the enclosure

parts.note: PS, a postscript, adds afterthoughts to a letter
Noah's ark housed animals

explanation.surface: Reconsidering a zoo pen in civic spaces.
explanation.walkthrough: PS goes about ARK.
explanation.definitionFit: Parks are open green spaces for the public.

clue.text: Commotion about a stage of the flight

indicators.note: the word for commotion surrounds the letter

parts.note: a stir is a commotion

explanation.surface: Fuss about a part of an aircraft journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' is a flight of steps, not an air journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A single step is one of a staircase's units.

clue.text: Beds possibly have an effect unknown

parts.note: to count is to matter or have an effect
y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Perhaps beds make a difference nobody can quantify.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beds' is Bedfordshire, an English county, not furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedfordshire, abbreviated Beds, is an English shire.

clue.text: Jam car-starter with piece of wood

parts.note: the first letter of car
a log is a piece of wood

explanation.surface: Wedge a car's starter motor with a block of wood.
explanation.definitionFit: To clog is to block or obstruct.

clue.text: Pays further attention to a pupil's practice session

parts.note: to re-hear is to listen again
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A teacher listens more closely to a student's practice.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the British learner-driver plate letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a run-through before a performance.

clue.text: Notes about alternative worship

indicators.note: the notes wrap around the word for alternative

parts.note: A, D and E are musical notes
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Musical notes on another form of devotion.
explanation.walkthrough: Three notes, A, D and E, go around OR.
explanation.definitionFit: To adore is to revere or idolise.

clue.text: Deliver plant without-charge

parts.note: to set is to plant
free means costing nothing

explanation.surface: Bring a seedling round at no cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliver' means release, not bring round.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver someone is to liberate or rescue them.

clue.text: Small-time collector, one inclined to go after gems initially

indicators.note: the second piece is placed after the first
initially picks the opening letter of gems

parts.note: a leaner is one who leans, or is inclined

explanation.surface: A petty collector likes to pursue jewels first.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleaner gathers leftover grain or scraps bit by bit.
